To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protein composition of the teneral Glossina m. morsitan peritrophic matrix was determined for the first time.

the tsetse peritrophic matrix is composed of a large array of novel and previously described proteins, and that the secondary endosymbiotic bacterium, Sodalis, is closely associated with the peritrophic matrix.
we identified 300 proteins in the PM of teneral tsetse, several of those with CBDs, and that Sodalis is associated with the PM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underpin tsetse fly biology and how these may be exploited for trypanosome control.
identifying the proteins that make up the tsetse peritrophic matrix, and determining their role in the development of the trypanosomes within the midgut of the tsetses.
the molecular mechanisms of trypanosome infection in tsetse flies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein composition of the tsetsee PM is complex and that the proteins identified may have a variety of functions, which may include the adhesion of trypanosomes to the PM.
this study has identified the protein components that are likely to be responsible for the structural integrity and function of the tsetsee PM.
the PM of teneral Gmm contains several novel proteins, some of which are likely to be involved in trypanosome penetration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study is an important contribution to the tsetse biology field.
we identified a total of 300 proteins from teneral Glossina m. morsitan PMs, which is the first time this has been done in this fly.
we have identified the protein components of the tsetsetse peritrophic matrix, which may help in understanding the mechanism of trypanosome penetration and migration through this structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PM is not a static structure, but a dynamic entity that undergoes changes during teneral development.
the PM of the teneral G. moristans morsitens is a dynamic protein complex that is likely to play a key role during trypanosome infection.

the tsetse peritrophic matrix is an extremely complex structure and that the PM is probably not only involved in the protection of the midgut from the deleterious effect of the ingested bloodmeal, but also in the regulation of the tsetsetransmitted pathogens, as it may play a role in trypanosome migration and/or development.
